name: XML
typing: schema-typed (DTD attribute types, external schema languages)
summary: A simplified profile of SGML standardised by the W3C: a Unicode text syntax for labelled trees of elements, attributes and character data, with entities, DTD validation, and a family of companion specifications (Namespaces, Infoset, XInclude, xml:id, canonicalization). The substrate of XHTML, SVG, SOAP, office formats and countless configuration and interchange vocabularies.

level_notes.0: No reference implementation exists; conformance is defined by the W3C/NIST/OASIS XML Conformance Test Suite. The dominant parsers are linked: libxml2 and Expat (C), Xerces (Java/C++, also inside the JDK), plus the standard-library parsers of Python, Go, .NET and several Rust/JS/OCaml implementations that differ in which optional features (DTD, external entities, namespaces) they implement.
level_notes.1: XML 1.0 Fifth Edition is the normative core; it embeds the DTD language (catalogued separately as `dtd`). www.w3.org answers this catalog's link checker with HTTP 403 (reported `blocked`); every W3C anchor below was verified by fetching the page with a different client. Namespaces, Infoset, XML Base, xml:id, XInclude and Canonical XML are separate Recommendations layered on the core; XSD, RELAX NG, XPath, XSLT and XQuery have their own catalog entries.
level_notes.2: Secondary literature is vast but much of the classic material (IBM developerWorks, Sun, Cover Pages) has moved or vanished; surviving canonical items (Bray's Annotated XML, Harold's books, TEI's Gentle Introduction, platform parser guides, security cheat sheets) are linked.
level_notes.3: Wikipedia has separate articles for most sub-topics (namespaces, DTD, CDATA, entity attacks), linked individually because they are section-level tertiary sources.
